questions.question: Two connected servers both expose a tool named search. What goes wrong if the host flattens all tools into one list?
options: One of them is hidden or the model calls the wrong one
questions.explanation: Namespacing (server__tool) makes every exposed name unique.

questions.question: Why does the hub use two underscores, as in files__search, rather than files/search?
options: Tool names must stick to letters, digits, _, - and ., and many model APIs are stricter
questions.explanation: The exposed name has to be valid for both MCP and the model's tool format.

questions.question: Fifteen tools from six servers cost about 850 tokens per turn. What does per-task selection buy?
options: Nothing; models handle any number of tools
Less context spent and fewer similar tools for the model to confuse
questions.explanation: Here it went from 15 tools to the 6 the task needed.

questions.question: The calendar server is slow. How does the hub stop it holding up a files call made in the same turn?
options: Calls to different servers run in parallel, each with its own timeout; a timeout becomes an error observation
questions.explanation: Separate processes, separate readers, separate deadlines.

questions.question: A server crashes on every call. What should the host do?
options: Remove its tools, keep the others working, restart a limited number of times, then leave it down and report why
questions.explanation: A restart budget avoids endless crash loops.

questions.question: Results from many servers now share one model context. What new risk does that create?
options: Text returned by one server can steer the model's calls to another server
questions.explanation: Cross-server injection is covered in Lesson 11.
